What is the first question of the system-analysis method?
column2: Which constraint binds first: energy, heat, bandwidth, latency, cost or reliability. A budget for that currency, block by block, shows which term dominates and which knob moves the answer most.

column1: How does battery power relate to load powers through a converter chain?
column2: P_batt = Σ P_k/η_k, so every watt delivered through an η-efficient converter costs 1/η watts from the battery; the system efficiency is Σ P_k/P_batt.

column1: Why is an LDO a poor choice for a large step-down?
column2: Its efficiency is at most V_out/V_in, because the load current flows through it at the full input voltage; a 3.8 V to 1.8 V LDO wastes more than half its input.

column1: What sets a device's sustained power?
column2: Heat leaving the case: P_sus = (T_s,max − T_a)/θ_sa. The chip's own rating is irrelevant once the case or skin limit binds.

column1: How long can a burst run before the case reaches its limit?
column2: t_b = τ ln[(T∞ − T0)/(T∞ − T_s,max)] with T∞ = T_a + P_b θ_sa and τ = θ_sa C_th: the burst borrows the case's thermal capacitance.

column1: What burst duty cycle keeps the average at the sustained limit?
column2: d_max = (P_sus − P_i)/(P_b − P_i), with idle power P_i and burst power P_b.

column1: What is gross margin?
column2: (ASP − COGS)/ASP, with COGS = BOM + other unit costs; a cent of BOM matters in proportion to volume divided by ASP.

column1: How does the roofline bound attainable performance?
column2: P_att = min(Π, Iβ): peak compute Π or arithmetic intensity I times bandwidth β, whichever is lower.

column1: What bounds LLM decode speed on a device?
column2: Memory bandwidth: tokens/s ≈ β/(N_p b), because every token reads all N_p parameters of b bytes each.

column1: What is the shadow price of a watt under a power cap?
column2: With P ∝ f³, d ln(perf)/dP = 1/(3P_dyn); a wider core pays only if its performance gain g exceeds its power ratio p to the one-third power.

column1: Why does energy per instruction have a minimum in frequency?
column2: Dynamic energy per instruction c(V0 + kf)²/IPC rises with f, while leakage energy per instruction P_s/(IPC·f) falls; the optimum solves 2ck(V0 + kf*)f*² = P_s.

column1: Why run below the energy-optimal frequency only when forced?
column2: Below f*, leakage per instruction grows faster than dynamic energy falls, so going slower costs energy as well as time.

column1: How is DRAM bandwidth computed from the interface?
column2: β = R·w/8 bytes per second, with transfer rate R and bus width w bits.

column1: What does a system-level cache do for DRAM traffic?
column2: Each agent's DRAM traffic is its demand times (1 − hit rate); summing gives the load on the shared memory interface.

column1: Why are phone SoCs heterogeneous?
column2: Different work has different energy-optimal engines: big and little CPU cores, GPU, NPU, ISP and DSPs each do their task at lower energy per operation than a general core.

column1: What usually limits a phone's sustained performance?
column2: The few watts the case can shed at a comfortable skin temperature, not the silicon's peak; bursts exceed it briefly.

column1: Why is the modem integrated or closely coupled with the AP?
column2: Shared memory, power management and a smaller board save energy and cost, at the price of design complexity and supplier concentration.

column1: What does the ISP do and why is it dedicated hardware?
column2: It turns raw sensor data into images (demosaic, noise reduction, tone mapping) at hundreds of megapixels per second, which a CPU could not do within the power budget.

column1: How is a smartwatch's battery life computed?
column2: L = 24 h × u η E_b / E_day, with E_day = Σ P_i t_i over the day's modes, usable fraction u and conversion efficiency η.

column1: What is the luminous flux of a Lambertian emitter of area A and luminance L_v?
column2: Φ = π L_v A; display power is π L_v A · APL/η_v.

column1: Why do LTPO displays save power on a watch?
column2: Oxide transistors leak so little that a pixel holds its charge long enough (t_hold = C_st ΔV/I_off) to refresh at 1 Hz in always-on mode.

column1: Why batch sensor samples before waking the application processor?
column2: P_AP(N) = f_s E_s + f_s E_w/N: the wake-up energy is shared by N samples, up to the latency limit N ≤ f_s τ.

column1: When does a sensor hub beat batching on the AP?
column2: When the hub's own power plus its per-sample and per-result energies, P_h + f_s E_h + r E_w, is below the batched AP's power.

column1: What sets the charge of a BLE connection event?
column2: Q_ev = I_pre t_pre + I_rx (t_rx + T_IFS) + I_tx t_tx; the average current is the sleep floor plus window widening plus Q_ev/T.

column1: Why does a longer BLE connection interval stop helping?
column2: The average current approaches the sleep floor plus the receiver's window-widening term, which do not shrink with the interval.

column1: What is cold brownout?
column2: At low temperature the cell's internal resistance rises, so V_t = V_oc − I R_int sags under a current pulse and can trip the undervoltage reset before the battery is empty.

column1: How much electrical power does a speaker need for a given loudness?
column2: P = 1 mW × 10^((SPL − S)/10) for sensitivity S in dB SPL per mW: every 10 dB louder costs ten times the power.

column1: Why does delay limit active noise cancellation?
column2: The anti-noise arrives τ late, leaving a residual |R| = 2|sin(πfτ)|; attenuation falls with frequency and turns into amplification above 1/(6τ).

column1: What limits ANC at low frequency?
column2: Gain error: with no delay the residual is |1 − g|, so 30 dB needs the gain right to about 3%.

column1: How many full recharges does an earbud case give?
column2: N = η_t E_case/(2E_b): the case's delivered energy divided by the energy of both buds.

column1: What limits always-on compute in smart glasses?
column2: Heat: the frame can shed only hA ΔT at a skin-safe temperature rise, a fraction of a watt.

column1: Why do waveguide displays need efficient light engines?
column2: Display power is L_v·APL/(η_wg η_src), and waveguides deliver few nits per lumen, so brightness outdoors costs heavily.

column1: What does foveated rendering save?
column2: Shading work w = x + (1 − x)s², with x the foveal area fraction and s the peripheral linear resolution scale.

column1: Why does motion-to-photon latency matter in XR?
column2: Registration error is ωτ: at fast head turns even a few milliseconds misplace virtual objects; reprojection and pose prediction hide part of the pipeline.

column1: How is a laptop SoC's average power computed?
column2: By residency: P̄ = Σ r_i P_i over power states, plus the display; battery life is the battery energy over the total.

column1: How long can a laptop chip run at PL2?
column2: t = τ ln[(P2 − P0)/(P2 − P1)], the time an exponentially weighted moving average starting at P0 takes to reach PL1 under P2.

column1: What bounds local LLM decode on a laptop?
column2: Memory bandwidth: tokens/s ≤ BW/(N_p b/8), with b bits per parameter; unified memory width and speed set it.

column1: What bounds prefill?
column2: Compute: t_prefill = 2N_p T/(TOPS × u) for T prompt tokens at utilization u.

column1: Why might a laptop SoC use chiplets?
column2: Smaller dies yield better and can use different processes, but packaging, die-to-die links and assembly yield add cost: C = (Σ C_die + C_pkg)/Y_asm.

column1: Why does deep idle matter more than peak power for battery life?
column2: Most of a laptop's day is spent idle or light, so residency-weighted power is dominated by low states and the display.

column1: What does memory on package buy?
column2: Shorter, lower-capacitance links with less energy per bit and board area, at the cost of fixed capacity per SKU.

column1: Why can a CAN node with the lowest identifier win arbitration without corrupting the frame?
column2: The bus is wired-AND: dominant (0) overrides recessive (1), and a node that sends recessive but reads dominant stops transmitting.

column1: What is the worst-case length of a classic CAN frame with n data bytes?
column2: 34 + 8n + 13 + ⌊(34 + 8n − 1)/4⌋ bits, including worst-case stuff bits; 135 bits for 8 bytes.

column1: How is a CAN message's worst-case response time found?
column2: Iterate R_i = B_i + C_i + Σ_hp ⌈(w_i + τ_bit)/T_j⌉ C_j: blocking, its own frame, and higher-priority frames released during its wait.

column1: Why do response times explode near full bus load?
column2: Waiting lengthens the window in which more higher-priority frames arrive, a feedback that makes the busy period grow much faster than load.

column1: What dominates a car's sensor data rate?
column2: Cameras: R = pixels × frame rate × bits per pixel, gigabits per second each, far above radar or lidar.

column1: What share of an EV's range does a computer cost?
column2: P_c/(P_c + P_d) with driving power P_d = e·v: largest in slow city traffic.

column1: How does latency affect stopping distance?
column2: d_stop = vt + v²/(2a): every 100 ms at highway speed adds several metres.

column1: What does diagnostic coverage achieve?
column2: A residual failure rate λ(1 − DC) that must fit the ASIL budget; it detects faults but does not keep the function working.

column1: What is a zonal E/E architecture?
column2: Zone controllers near the devices, connected by a backbone to central computers, replacing one ECU per function; it saves wiring and consolidates software.

column1: How should a rack datasheet be read?
column2: Divide totals by device count; check whether link bandwidth counts both directions; normalize compute to one precision without sparsity.

column1: What is machine balance and why do accelerators converge on it?
column2: Peak FLOP/s over memory bandwidth; dense FP8 balances of different vendors are close because they share HBM technology.

column1: Why is all-in power per accelerator larger than the chip rating?
column2: CPUs, memory, NICs, switches, conversion losses, fans and PUE add to the GPU's own power.

column1: Where does training compute 6ND come from?
column2: Per weight per token: 2 FLOPs forward, 2 for the input gradient and 2 for the weight gradient.

column1: What is model FLOPs utilization?
column2: Useful model FLOPs achieved over peak; it absorbs stalls, communication, bubbles and imbalance and is often under half at scale.

column1: What is the ring all-reduce time?
column2: 2(p − 1)/p · S/B + 2(p − 1)α: the bandwidth term is nearly independent of p, the latency term grows with p.

column1: Why does a large scale-up domain help data-parallel training?
column2: In a hierarchical all-reduce each device's network port carries only 1/p1 of the gradient, so the domain acts as one pipe of p1 times the port bandwidth.

column1: Why do big training jobs fail often?
column2: With N independent components of MTBF m, the job's mean time between failures is m/N.

column1: What is Young's checkpoint interval?
column2: τ* = √(2δM), balancing save overhead δ/τ against rework τ/(2M); the lost fraction is √(2δ/M) + R/M.

column1: What limits a rack's decode throughput as the batch grows?
column2: Each sequence's KV cache: throughput approaches ηB_mem/K, and per-user speed falls along a line of slope W/K.

column1: What dominates the cost per token?
column2: Capital, through utilization and batch; electricity is typically a minority share.

column1: Why do microcontroller networks use depthwise-separable convolutions?
column2: They cut MACs and weights to 1/C_out + 1/k² of a standard convolution, about eight times for 3 × 3 kernels and 64 channels.

column1: Why is an NPU's speed-up on a small model below its peak MAC ratio?
column2: Depthwise and small layers leave the MAC array underused; utilization, not peak, sets the gain.

column1: What dominates an always-on device's power after adding an NPU?
column2: Often the sensor front end and feature extraction: P_avg = rE_inf + P_fe + P_sleep.

column1: When should an edge device compute locally?
column2: When inference energy plus the radio energy of the result is less than the radio energy of the raw data; on long-range links it is also the only way to fit the bandwidth.

column1: What is LoRa's symbol time?
column2: T_s = 2^SF/BW: each spreading-factor step doubles it, roughly doubling airtime and energy for about 2.5 dB more sensitivity.

column1: What does a 1% duty cycle allow?
column2: 36 seconds of transmission per hour per sub-band in the EU 868 MHz band.

column1: Why can self-discharge set a sensor's life?
column2: A node using a joule or two a day loses a comparable amount to the cell's self-discharge, so the battery ages out first.

column1: How is indoor PV power estimated from lux?
column2: P = (E_v/K)A η_pv η_c: illuminance over luminous efficacy gives irradiance, times area and efficiencies.

column1: How is a supercapacitor sized for a dark period?
column2: C = 2E/(V_max² − V_min²), with E the load energy over the longest dark period, usually a weekend.

column1: Why are firmware updates a system cost on LoRaWAN?
column2: A full image is thousands of frames: minutes of airtime, joules of receive energy and far more downlink time than duty cycles allow per day.

column1: What does the EU Cyber Resilience Act require of connected products?
column2: Security requirements, vulnerability reporting and security updates over a support period, in most cases at least five years.
